title: Grab And Move should work with TouchScreen & Stylus
author: JimR-15
summary: The report asks Grab and Move to support touchscreen and stylus input, which is a new input-modality feature request rather than evidence that existing mouse dragging regressed.

status.label: Feature request, not current bug
status.detail: Touch and pen support require product and interaction design for gestures, pointer capture, and conflicts with normal touch scrolling/selection.

next_action.label: Clarify feature classification
next_action.reason: Route the request as an enhancement without asking the reporter to prove unsupported touch/stylus behavior as a regression.

judgment.rationale: The issue requests support for Win+touch and Win+stylus drag to match the existing modifier+mouse behavior. The implementation currently handles low-level mouse messages, and the report does not identify a previously supported touch or pen path that stopped working.
evidence: The body describes a Framework 12 touchscreen/stylus scenario and says Win+Touchscreen and Win+Stylus drag do nothing.
The expected behavior asks touchscreen, touchpad, mouse, and stylus to all drag windows once the activation modifier is pressed.
No prior working version, regression boundary, diagnostic archive, comments, assignee, or linked implementation is present.
Code inspection of src/modules/GrabAndMove/GrabAndMove/main.cpp found low-level mouse handling for WM_LBUTTONDOWN, WM_MOUSEMOVE, and WM_LBUTTONUP, not a touch/stylus pointer path.
judgment.recommended_action: Reclassify/evaluate as an enhancement covering touch and pen gesture design, pointer input plumbing, and interaction conflicts.

issue_context.summary: Grab and Move currently lacks the touch and stylus interaction requested by the reporter.
known_information: The requested input devices are touchscreen and stylus on a Framework 12 convertible laptop.
The existing working interaction is modifier key plus mouse drag.
The report does not identify a version in which touch or stylus dragging previously worked.
No comments, attachments, assignees, linked work, or direct duplicate are present.
inferences: Adding touch and pen support would require defining gestures, pointer capture, scrolling conflicts, and accessibility behavior rather than repairing a demonstrated regression.
The current low-level mouse-hook implementation is not evidence of a broken touch/stylus path; it suggests the path was never implemented.
issue_context.analysis: The request is clear enough to classify without diagnostics. Treating it as a feature request preserves the product-design question and avoids a misleading bug-fix design loop.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full live issue, comments, labels, assignees, timeline, and closed-by-PR references.
Searched duplicate candidates and found only the current issue for the same Grab and Move touch/stylus wording.
Inspected the Grab and Move low-level input path in main.cpp, which handles mouse messages for modifier+button dragging.

actions.label: Post feature-request guidance

comment.body: Thanks for the suggestion. Touchscreen and stylus support would add new input modalities to Grab and Move rather than fix a demonstrated regression in its current mouse interaction. This should be evaluated as a feature request, including the intended touch/pen gesture, interaction with normal scrolling and selection, and accessibility requirements.
